summary: Discovery/POC scoping for claims-processing and document search use cases. Discussed workload sizing, success criteria (p95 latency <300ms for short prompts, acceptable cost targets, throughput target ~100 req/s), and deployment decision criteria (Hosted for fast start, Dedicated for predictable latency/cost, Private for strict data residency/KMS). Agreed Redwood will run benchmarks against a 10k prompt sample and propose sizing/pricing; 4-week POC timeline was proposed with security review parallelized.
topics: deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-05 15:30 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Quasar Head of AI), Priya Rao (Quasar Platform Lead), Mark Delgado (Security)

Summary: Short discovery focusing on POC scoping for claims triage and search. Conversation covered SLOs, throughput, dataset samples, and security hurdles to pick between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.

00:00 Liam: hey everyone, thanks for making time. we've been looking at redwood as an option for our claims automation and retrieval use cases. main ask is fast triage + secure embeddings for internal search
00:28 Maya: great to meet you all, i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, arjun our solutions engineer is here to dig into sizing and benchmarks, quick quick question on current stack what are you running today?
00:45 Priya: we run most services on aws, EKS clusters, some on-prem for legacy systems, we use s3 for storage, and our models for heuristics live in a mix of lambda and EC2. we also have an on-prem data store with PHI so data residency is a thing
01:10 Arjun: got it, thanks. for the POC are you mostly looking to call generation/chat endpoints or embeddings for search, or both?
01:22 Liam: both — embeddings for document search and rerank, and generation for triage/initial summary. latency is important for triage flow, we'd like p95 sub-300ms for short prompts ideally, but we'll trade cost if needed
01:40 Maya: that's a helpful target. typical Q we ask — what's your expected concurrency/throughput? that informs batching and whether Dedicated is needed
01:52 Priya: nightly batch jobs are easy, but for realtime triage we expect bursts of 80-120 reqs per second during peak business hours, average 25-30 reqs/s
02:15 Arjun: ok that maps to needing predictable per-request latency. with hosted shared pools you can hit variability in p95 under bursty loads unless there's burst capacity; Dedicated helps with the predictable throughput and consistent latency
02:35 Mark: and from security side our constraints — SOC2 type II is must, keys must be customer-managed KMS for any PHI, VPC peering or private link is preferred, and we need audit logs retained for 12 months
02:55 Maya: totally reasonable. we have Hosted with standard policies, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict isolation. i'll ask arjun to walk through tradeoffs
03:10 Arjun: sure. high level: Hosted = fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, less upfront sizing; Dedicated = reserved capacity, predictable latency and cost, can pin models and kernels; Private = full network isolation, customer-controlled keys and audit plane but longer lead time and infra ops on your side
03:40 Liam: what kind of lead time for Private? our security team will be strict
03:50 Arjun: Private deployments typically 6-12 weeks depending on on-prem work and approvals; Dedicated can be online in 2-4 weeks with reserved capacity; Hosted is immediate once accounts are provisioned
04:10 Priya: for cost sensitivity, can you give a rough comparison? i know it depends on usage but a ballpark helps
04:22 Maya: rough rule: Hosted has the highest variability but lowest up-front; Dedicated lowers unit cost at scale because you pay for reserved GPUs; Private has similar infra cost to Dedicated plus integration and ops overhead. we'll send a sizing worksheet to estimate committed capacity vs on-demand mix
04:45 Arjun: for the POC we'll propose a small Dedicated footprint to run the benchmark and can fallback to Hosted early if you want a faster pilot. benchmarks let us quantify p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens for each mode
05:05 Liam: sounds good. what's in the benchmark?
05:12 Arjun: plan is: you provide 10k representative prompts and top-k documents for embedding similarity tests. we'll run: 1) latency profile for short/long prompts, 2) throughput ramp (1 to 200 concurrent requests), 3) embedding recall/latency tests, 4) resource utilization. we recommend a 2-hour load window for throughput and a separate 1-hour accuracy pass for embeddings
05:45 Priya: expected datasets might have PII and PHI, can we scrub before sending?
05:52 Maya: yes scrub if needed, but also we can run a hashed/anonymized sample — whatever your compliance team requires. for security review we'll share SOC2, encryption, and on-prem docs
06:10 Mark: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys in Hosted? or only in Private?
06:18 Arjun: we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption and we have customer key options depending on plan — we'll include specifics in the security packet
06:35 Liam: what's the success criteria you'd propose for the POC?
06:40 Maya: from what you said we'd propose: 1) p95 latency for triage <300ms for short prompts in Dedicated config, 2) embedding recall within 3% of your current baseline, 3) throughput able to sustain 100 req/s at p95 SLO, 4) security signoff on KMS/audit/logs and VPC connectivity
07:05 Priya: timeline? we need to align with our sprint cadence
07:10 Maya: proposed POC timeline: Week 0 (this week) — finalize scope and dataset, Week 1 — Redwood config and Dedicated staging cluster + security onboarding, Week 2 — benchmark runs and tuning, Week 3 — evaluate results and provide recommendations, Week 4 — decision and next steps. so roughly a 4-week POC
07:35 Liam: ok that aligns with our next quarter planning. budget holder is procurement, likely a mid-size committed spend if Dedicated makes sense
08:00 Arjun: technical deep-dive — for latency we recommend using model variants and quantization profiles. Dedicated lets us pick kernels and keep KV cache warm; Hosted can do some caching but less predictable due to multi-tenant pools
08:25 Priya: can Redwood integrate with our EKS for routing? we prefer traffic to stay in VPC where possible
08:33 Arjun: yes for Dedicated/Private we can peer or use private link; we have an EKS connector pattern for routing requests to on-prem or vpc endpoints; details in the integration guide we'll share
08:50 Mark: audit log retention — do you offer configurable retention windows? 12 months is our minimum
08:58 Maya: yes configurable, it's an add-on for longer retention but 12 months is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted may have different tiers but we'll include an SLA note
09:15 Liam: any reference customers in insurance or regulated sectors?
09:20 Maya: we've worked with a couple of insurers and healthcare customers — i'll share anonymized case studies and a contact who can speak to Dedicated deployment
09:35 Priya: what's the fallback policy if Dedicated capacity saturates in peak?
09:42 Arjun: we support automatic overflow to compatible Hosted pools when configured as a fallback, with scrubbing of context if required. that keeps the app online with graceful degradation
10:00 Liam: important to know — we plan to run an offline accuracy test first then live traffic with a canary 5% rollout
10:10 Maya: good plan. will include canary rollout recommendations and monitoring hooks in the runbook we send
10:25 Mark: legal will want to review data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses for cross-border data transfer
10:32 Maya: we have templates and can share the DPA and SCCs; we'll flag anything specific for Private deployments
10:45 Arjun: technical note on benchmarks — to model production, include real token distribution and average sequence lengths; that drives kernel selection and batching behavior
11:05 Liam: what metrics will you return from the benchmark?
11:10 Arjun: we'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, estimated cost per 1M tokens, and embedding recall/precision against your baseline; we'll also provide recommended batch sizes and quantization profiles per model
11:35 Priya: for embedding recall threshold — what's acceptable?
11:40 Maya: usually within 2-5% of baseline is reasonable for production acceptance, we'll let you set the exact SLA for the POC
12:00 Liam: ok, to recap — you will send sizing/pricing, security docs, and schedule the benchmark; we will send sample prompts and traffic histograms, security will confirm KMS/audit needs
12:20 Maya: yep and propose we do the benchmark next wednesday (2026-03-11) if that works for your ops team
12:35 Liam: works for us, i'll confirm offline and share the dataset by monday
12:50 Maya: great. thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and invite for the benchmark calendar event
13:05 End of call
